title: Aaron’s feast: Cras solemnitas Jehovae—honor of the cast image referred to the true patriarchal God
source_text: XXIX. Similiter quum Aaron, in honorem vituli a se fusi, festum indixit, praeconis voce clamavit, Cras solemnitas Domini est. Ubi textus Hebraeus habet, Cras solemnitas est Jehovae, quod nomen proprium est veri illius Dei, quem Patriarchae coluerunt. Argumento manifesto, Israelitas ad verum Patrum suorum Deum retulisse honorem illum, quem imagini a se conflatae exhibebant.
pass_a_gloss: Likewise when Aaron, in honor of the calf cast by himself, proclaimed a feast, he cried with a herald’s voice, Tomorrow is the solemnity of the Lord. Where the Hebrew text has, Tomorrow is the solemnity of Jehovah, which is the proper name of that true God whom the Patriarchs cultivated. By a manifest argument, that the Israelites referred that honor which they exhibited to the image cast by themselves to the true God of their Fathers.
pass_b_english: Aaron’s proclamation names Jehovah’s feast, not a rival god’s.
So the calf-honor was explicitly referred to the patriarchal true God.

choices.why: Jehovah as the true God’s own name.
